bifrost: none for GSS-API. Adjacent: springboard/src/keychain.rs, springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (generic password items, not GSS credentials), springboard/src/net/wifi_config.rs (Wi-Fi Enterprise EAP settings, not GSS)
summary: Apple's GSS framework is the GSS-API (RFC 2743/2744) for Kerberos-style authenticated sessions, message protection and name handling. BifrOSt has no GSS-API implementation, no Kerberos or krb5 code and no SDK surface for it. The only nearby work is the per-app keychain for stored passwords and Wi-Fi Enterprise (EAP) settings, which do not perform GSS security-context exchange.

features.apple: gss_release_buffer, gss_release_oid_set, GSS object release functions (Allocating and Releasing Objects)
features.note: Rust ownership replaces GSS release calls; no GSS objects exist to release

features.apple: GSS_S_COMPLETE, GSS_S_FAILURE, GSS_C_MECH_CODE, gss_display_status, GSSCreateError (Function Status)
features.note: Wave 3 (w3-gss, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. keychain errors use OSStatus-style codes only; there is no GSS major/minor status model

features.feature: Buffer management (gss_buffer_desc, buffer sets, IOV buffers)
features.note: Wave 3 (w3-gss, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no GSS buffer descriptors; apps use Rust slices and Vec
no security-context negotiation code in springboard/ or the SDK

Wave 4 (w4-gss, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. the keychain stores app secrets as (service, account) items; it does not acquire, inquire or refresh Kerberos or GSS credentials
no mechanism registry; no SASL mapping

Wave 3 (theme-23, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no ASN.1 OID handling in the SDK or shell
Wave 4 (w4-gss, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no GSS token framing

features.apple: gss_wrap, gss_unwrap, gss_get_mic, gss_verify_mic, gss_seal, gss_unseal, gss_sign (Message Protection)
features.bifrost: springboard/src/keychain.rs (ChaCha20 and HMAC-SHA256 for keychain files at rest)
features.note: the keychain file cipher is local storage protection with a per-app key; it is not GSS per-message wrap or MIC and cannot be used as one

features.feature: Kerberos implementation (gss_krb5_*, lucid context, acceptor identity)
features.note: no Kerberos or krb5 code in the repo (grep for kerberos, gssapi, gss_, krb5, spnego over the whole tree returns no GSS hits); no KDC or ticket cache support

gaps: No GSS-API (RFC 2743/2744) implementation: no security contexts, credentials, names, tokens or message protection.
No Kerberos (krb5) client or ticket cache, so enterprise Kerberos sign-in and SPNEGO/Negotiate HTTP auth are unavailable to apps.
No SDK API for app-level GSS credentials; the keychain (springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs) stores generic passwords only.
No mechanism or name registry (gss_indicate_mechs, GSSCreateName), so apps cannot select or compare authentication mechanisms.
Wi-Fi Enterprise (EAP) credentials in springboard/src/net/wifi_config.rs are a separate 802.1X path and are not a GSS counterpart.
